en.title: Number of Failures Because a Prerequisite Has Not Run Yet
en.description:
Both arrays are permutations of 1..n, giving the prescribed order and the actual execution order respectively. When a process runs, it fails if any process prescribed before it has not run yet. A process that has already run but failed no longer counts as not yet run, so failures do not propagate.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..200000), followed by two lines: the prescribed permutation and the actual permutation.
en.explanation: Example 1: 4 runs last, so the other five processes all miss the prerequisite 4; the answer is 5. Example 2: the orders match, so the answer is 0. Example 3: when 5 runs, 2 and 3 are missing, and when 4 runs, 1 is missing; only these two fail, so the answer is 2.
hints: Record each process's actual position and scan in the prescribed order; if the current position is less than the maximum actual position seen so far, at least one prerequisite runs after it.
